articles.title: The Room That Forgot You: A Museum Mystery with an Archivist That Runs in Your Browser
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. The museum knows every donor's name. It cannot tell you who washed the cups. The Room That Forgot You…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built The museum knows every donor's name. It cannot tell you who washed the cups. The Room That Forgot You is a first-person browser mystery set in a railway museum after closing. Its archivist remembers important visitors and celebrated events. Someone else survives only in the margins: an extra cup, repeated return tickets, handwriting beneath an official signature. You enter with a flashlight and a handheld receiver. Your job is to give that person a place in the record. The main mechanic is evidence changing the room . Finding a document is only the beginning. Connect it to another record, establish what happened, and confirm the connection.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built Digital Séance is an AI-powered supernatural storytelling application that transforms ordinary memories, diary entries, and fictional scenarios into mysterious ghost stories. Inspired by Halloween and the idea of preserving stories from the past, I wanted to create something that combines supernatural storytelling with open-source artificial intelligence. Users can enter a memory or a fictional situation, choose a supernatural personality, select a storytelling tone, and generate an atmospheric story. The experience includes different spirit personalities, alternate endings, mysterious messages, and a personal story archive.

articles.title: HiveMQ vs Mosquitto: a tiny EPL broker or a clustered broker with published prices
articles.excerpt: HiveMQ and Eclipse Mosquitto both speak MQTT 5, 3.1.1 and 3.1, and both have a free open-source broker. They sit at opposite ends of the scale, though: Mosquitto is a small broker that runs almost any…
articles.body: HiveMQ and Eclipse Mosquitto both speak MQTT 5, 3.1.1 and 3.1, and both have a free open-source broker. They sit at opposite ends of the scale, though: Mosquitto is a small broker that runs almost anywhere, while HiveMQ is a clustered enterprise broker with published prices. Open-source option HiveMQ has a Community Edition: Java-based, Apache-2.0, with full MQTT 3.x and 5 support. Mosquitto is open source as a whole, under EPL-2.0 or EDL-1.0 (SPDX: EPL-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause). Pricing (as of Oct 2026) HiveMQ self-managed publishes monthly prices: a free Lab license (1 broker, 25 connections, 30 days, renewable at no charge), Launch at US$299/month (10,000 connections, 500 msg/s) and Run at US$499/month (10,000 connections, 1,000 msg/s). Enterprise is priced by connections and throughput.

articles.title: Node.js Error Tracking: Library Integration Practices for Safe Tenant Cohort Rollbacks
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a Node.js error tracking library when its triage workflow fits, or use a self-describing REST surface when the priority is integrating inference and telemetry with little glue; in bo…
articles.body: Short answer: use a Node.js error tracking library when its triage workflow fits, or use a self-describing REST surface when the priority is integrating inference and telemetry with little glue; in both cases, attach tenant and cohort context before deciding to roll back. For a healthtech experiment, error tracking is useful only if it helps answer a rollback question: did this tenant cohort fail because of the inference request, our application, or a missing downstream signal? The practical design is to capture exceptions with stable tenant and experiment context, connect the inference result to that event, and rehearse the rollback path with a deliberate test error. Start with the rollback rule. Telemetry is part of the rollback mechanism.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).
articles.body: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
